req.title: Set cookie via query string
req.statement: The system shall set cookies for every k=v pair supplied in the query string of GET /cookies/set.

doc.reasoning: The endpoint GET /cookies/set sets one cookie per k=v query parameter and redirects to /cookies. Tests must verify: (1) a single k=v pair sets exactly that cookie (EP positive), (2) multiple k=v pairs all get set (DT positive), (3) no query params yields no cookies set (BVA boundary), (4) a single param with empty value is accepted (BVA boundary), (5) the redirect target is exactly /cookies (STC state transition), and (6) the response without following redirects is a 302 not 200 (NEG negative path). Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (302 vs 200), exact cookie names and values, exact redirect Location header, and exact cookie counts.

tests.name: test_set_single_cookie_via_query_string
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
No pre-existing cookies in the test client
actions: Create a Flask test client with allow_redirects=False
GET /cookies/set?foo=bar
Assert the initial response is a 302 redirect
Follow the redirect to /cookies
Assert the JSON body contains exactly {"cookies": {"foo": "bar"}}
expected: cookies dict contains key 'foo' with value 'bar'
trace: R-HTTPBIN-031: system shall set cookies for every k=v pair in query string
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_set_single_cookie_via_query_string():
    r = client.get('/cookies/set?foo=bar', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/cookies'
    r2 = client.get('/cookies/set?foo=bar', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    data = r2.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'cookies' in data
    assert data['cookies'] == {'foo': 'bar'}
    assert len(data['cookies']) == 1

test_set_single_cookie_via_query_string()

from httpbin.core import app

def test_set_cookie_redirect_is_302_not_200():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/cookies/set?x=y', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 301
    assert r.status_code != 303
    loc = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert loc == '/cookies'

from httpbin.core import app

def test_set_cookie_value_is_exact_not_mutated():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/cookies/set?session=abc123', follow_redirects=True)

tests.name: test_set_cookie_state_transition_cookie_persists_to_view
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Test client maintains cookie jar across requests
actions: Create a fresh Flask test client
GET /cookies/set?tok=xyz with follow_redirects=True (sets cookie and lands on /cookies)
Then GET /cookies directly on the same client
Assert /cookies returns the same cookie 'tok'='xyz' set in the previous step
trace: R-HTTPBIN-031: cookie set via /cookies/set must be visible at /cookies endpoint
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_set_cookie_state_transition_cookie_persists_to_view():
    client = app.test_client()
    r1 = client.get('/cookies/set?tok=xyz', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    d1 = r1.get_json()
    assert d1['cookies'].get('tok') == 'xyz'
    r2 = client.get('/cookies')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    d2 = r2.get_json()
    assert d2 is not None
    assert 'cookies' in d2
    assert d2['cookies'].get('tok') == 'xyz'

test_set_cookie_state_transition_cookie_persists_to_view()
